Albania.visa: Unique residence permit for digital mobile workers (leje unike qendrimi per punonjes levizes digjital)
Albania.note: Law No. 79/2021 'On Foreigners' (consolidated 2025; Art. 68 amended by Law 43/2025 of 26.6.2025): issued for up to 1 year the first time to a foreigner lawfully in Albania who has an employment contract with an employer abroad or a service contract with a client abroad, sufficient income, accommodation, 1-year health insurance and a criminal record certificate.

Andorra.visa: Residence for digital nomads (D.3 Residencia per a nomada digital)
Andorra.note: Official e-tramits page: for people whose work needs no fixed location and uses telecoms; quota-limited (Decret 11/2023); at least 90 days a year in Andorra; first authorisation 2 years, renewals 2, 3, then 10 years; legal basis Llei 42/2022 (digital economy, entrepreneurship and innovation) plus the consolidated immigration law (Decret legislatiu 6-02-2019).

Anguilla.note: Unverifiable. Anguilla launched a remote-worker programme ('Lose the Crowd, Find Yourself', Work from Anguilla) in 2020, but the government Visas & Travel page does not mention it and the old application form (portal.ivisitanguilla.com/work-from-home-form/) now redirects to a 404. Could not confirm whether it still takes applications, nor the 'no progression to residence' claim. The Valley page presents the programme as current; worth checking by hand.

Aruba.note: No digital nomad visa. 'One Happy Workation' (Aruba Tourism Authority) is an accommodation-package programme for US nationals, 7 to 90 days, and the official page says it needs no governmental documentation. The Oranjestad page already describes this correctly.

Austria.note: The official migration portal's list of immigration types has no digital nomad or remote-work permit (Red-White-Red Card variants, self-employed key workers, start-up founders, ICT).

Azerbaijan.note: None in force. The State Programme for Tourism Development 2026-2030 (Presidential Order of 20 Aug 2026) tasks the MFA with studying a "digital traveller" e-visa subtype and drafting a Migration Code amendment: planned, not legislated. Baku sentence correct today.

Bangladesh.note: Embassy list of 15 visa categories, none for remote work; visa.gov.bd offers new visa, extension, NVR, on-arrival only. "None is under serious discussion" is not checkable.

Belarus.note: MFA visa purposes (diplomatic, service, business, sport/culture/science/education, humanitarian, religious, journalism, private, study, employment, tourism, permanent residence): no remote-work or nomad visa.

Belgium.note: No digital nomad permit; non-EU self-employed need the professional card. Beware: some sites (visasupdate.com, sapeople.com) report a 'Royal Decree of 2 August 2026' creating a Belgian nomad visa announced by 'State Secretary Mathieu Michel'; he left government on 3 February 2025, no official Belgian source mentions it, and Expatica (updated 30 June 2026) says none exists. Treat as false.

Bolivia.note: No digital nomad visa found in any source (secondary sources to July 2026 agree). Not confirmed against an official category list.

Bonaire.note: No remote-work permit in the Caribbean Netherlands. The tourist rule (Rijksdienst Caribisch Nederland): most foreign nationals up to 90 days every 180 days; European-Dutch, Caribbean-Dutch and US nationals up to 180 days every 365 days (90 days per 365 if they work or intern). So a short exit to Curacao does not extend a stay, which the Kralendijk sentence claims it does.

Bosnia and Herzegovina.note: Service for Foreigners' Affairs lists the temporary-residence grounds: family reunification, education, humanitarian, work with or without a work permit, other justified reasons, real-estate ownership. No nomad ground.

Brazil.visa: VITEM XIV (temporary visa for digital nomads)
Brazil.note: Resolucao CNIg MJSP 45 of 9 Sept 2021. For immigrants working remotely for a foreign employer, with no employment tie in Brazil. Proof of at least US$1,500 a month from a foreign source or US$18,000 in available funds, health insurance valid in Brazil, criminal record certificate. Initial residence up to 1 year, renewable for an equal period. Apply at a consulate before travel, or from inside Brazil as a residence authorisation from the Ministry of Justice and Public Security.

British Virgin Islands.note: No remote-work visa in force as of 2026. Ministers have discussed a long-stay / 'Invest and Stay' scheme, but no launch was found. gov.vg blocked automated fetches, so this rests on secondary sources dated to mid-2026.

Brunei.note: Visa types: diplomatic, social visit, professional visit, business visit, employment, dependent, student. Long Term Pass (https://www.immigration.gov.bn/long-term-pass/) has social, business and professional tracks only.

Bulgaria.visa: Residence permit for digital nomads (Art. 24(1) item 23, Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act)
Bulgaria.note: The official register of administrative services lists 'digital nomads' as a ground for a prolonged-residence permit under Art. 24(1) item 23 of the Foreigners Act, issued by the MoI Migration Directorate and regional migration offices. The Council of Ministers approved the application procedure (amended implementing regulations) on 10 December 2025 (government.bg agenda, item 13). Law amended in 2025; for people employed remotely by an employer outside the EU. Income figure and validity not verified on an official page.

Czech Republic.note: Not a separate visa type: a Ministry of Industry and Trade programme (2023, widened from 1 January 2025) giving IT and marketing specialists from 12 countries (AU, BR, CA, IL, JP, KR, MX, NZ, SG, UK, US, TW) fast access to a long-term visa for 'other' purposes (remote employees of foreign firms) or for business (trade licence). Germany.note: Official residence-type listings (Make it in Germany, Federal Foreign Office visa pages) contain no digital nomad or remote-work permit. The freelance permit (residence permit for self-employment / Freiberufler, s.21 AufenthG) is the route remote freelancers use.

Ghana.note: Ghana Immigration Service lists its services as eVisa, emergency entry, transit and re-entry visas, student/work/dependant residence permits, extensions, right of abode and indefinite residence. No remote-work or digital nomad category. Not in KPMG Jul 2026 or EY Mar 2026 either.

Greenland.note: SIRI: Greenland work permits generally require an employment agreement with a company registered in Greenland; no remote-work permit. (A SIRI visa-handbook line about a 'digital nomad' temporary stay visa that search tools attribute to Greenland is Portugal's Lei 18/22 entry.)

Grenada.note: Act No. 3 of 2021, assented 1 July 2021, in force 9 July 2021. The Chief Immigration Officer, with the Minister's approval, grants a remote-work permit valid up to one year, renewable for up to a year at a time. Conditions: no employment or business in Grenada, health insurance, police certificate, proof of actual annual income of at least EC$100,000 earned outside Grenada (about $37,000 at the fixed EC$2.70 peg). Dependants can be included. No repeal found; the Grenada Tourism Authority still promotes it. Not verified: whether applications are actively processed in 2026.

Guatemala.visa: Residencia temporal para trabajadores migrantes, con patrono extranjero (IGM)
Guatemala.note: Official IGM form 'IGM 01-2026', issued under Acuerdo IGM-016-2025 (Reglamento de Residencias Guatemaltecas, AMN 05-2025) and Codigo de Migracion arts. 75-77. Subcategory 'con patrono extranjero': bank statements showing pay from abroad of at least US$2,000 a month over the last year (US$3,000 with dependants), or a legalised/apostilled accountant's certificate; terms of 1, 2 or 3-5 years; filed in person at the Subdireccion de Extranjeria in Guatemala City. Not branded 'digital nomad' but it is a dedicated remote-worker residence route. Secondary sources date the regime to 8 Oct 2025; that date was not confirmed officially, so the fixes carry no date.

Peru.note: Decreto Legislativo 1582 (El Peruano, 14 Nov 2023) added art. 29.2(i) to DL 1350: a residence status for foreigners doing subordinate remote work for an employer domiciled abroad, with no Peruvian-source income, up to 365 days, extendable, granted by Migraciones, conditions to be 'fijadas en el Reglamento'. Migraciones' own news item (gob.pe 868954) says it will be granted once regulated. As of 2026 no regulation, TUPA procedure, requirements or fee has been published (2024 and 2025 TUPA updates omitted it per secondary sources). So it exists in law but cannot be applied for. Cusco, Mancora and Iquitos already say exactly this; the four that say Peru simply has none are fixed.

Philippines.visa: Digital Nomad Visa (DNV), Executive Order No. 86, s. 2025
Philippines.note: LEGISLATED BUT NOT OPEN. EO 86 signed 24 April 2025 authorises the DFA to issue DNVs to non-immigrant foreigners working remotely for clients/employers outside the Philippines: age 18+, proof of remote work and foreign income, no criminal record, health insurance, nationality of a country that offers DNVs to Filipinos and has a Philippine Foreign Service Post; stay up to 1 year, renewable. Sec. 7 required DFA guidelines within 30 days, but as of 2026-10-05 the DFA e-Visa portal (https://evisa.gov.ph/page/policy) lists only 9(a) temporary visitor visas, and no DFA, embassy or Bureau of Immigration page found mentions a DNV application. All 4 "no DNV" sentences are outdated: the visa exists in law but cannot be applied for.

Poland.note: No nomad visa. Poland.Business Harbour, which the Torun page presents as a live remote-work route, has been suspended by the Foreign Ministry since 26 January 2024 (consulates take no PBH applications); no resumption announced.

Qatar.note: Qatar Tourism's official visa page lists only visa-free entry (102 nationalities), visa on arrival with a Discover Qatar hotel booking, and Hayya A1/A2/A3 e-visas. No remote-work category; neither tracker lists Qatar. Reports of a planned nomad pathway are unofficial. The Doha sentence is only stale ('as of mid-2025').

Rwanda.note: Absence based only on two professional trackers (KPMG Digital Nomad and Remote Work visa options, 17 Jul 2026; EY Global Immigration Index: Remote Work and Digital Nomads, Mar 2026), neither of which lists this country; no official visa-type listing could be read, so no official verdict. The page sentences saying there is no such visa are consistent with that and were left alone. Kigali side claim "Rwanda has been updating employment regulations to be more accommodating of remote workers" could not be verified (migration.gov.rw pages render client-side).

Saint Barthelemy.note: French overseas collectivity; France has no digital nomad visa and Saint-Barthelemy has no separate one.

Saint Kitts and Nevis.note: No remote-work or digital nomad programme found on official channels. Secondary sites claiming a 2022 'Remote Work Stay' programme cite no government source and are contradicted by most others. Treated as none.

Saint Lucia.note: No dedicated remote-work visa. 'Live It' (launched 2021 by the Saint Lucia Tourism Authority) was a marketing programme built on the ordinary non-immigrant visa; its second phase used the multiple-entry visa valid one year (EC$190 per govt.lc). The stlucia.org Live It pages now return 404, consistent with the page saying it was not maintained. govt.lc does not state a per-visit stay length. All three Castries sentences judged correct.

Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.note: No remote-work or digital nomad programme found in any source; never introduced.

San Marino.note: Foreign ministry list of permessi di soggiorno and residenze (anagrafica, elettiva, atipica fiscale agevolata, atipica pensionati) has no remote-work category.

Sao Tome and Principe.note: Absence based only on two professional trackers (KPMG Digital Nomad and Remote Work visa options, 17 Jul 2026; EY Global Immigration Index: Remote Work and Digital Nomads, Mar 2026), neither of which lists this country; no official visa-type listing could be read, so no official verdict. The page sentences saying there is no such visa are consistent with that and were left alone.

Saudi Arabia.note: Official eVisa portal covers only the tourist eVisa (one year, multiple entry, up to 90 days, 68 eligible countries); the Premium Residency site (pr.gov.sa) renders client-side and could not be read. Neither tracker lists a Saudi nomad visa. Sentences consistent; no fix.

Senegal.note: Absence based only on two professional trackers (KPMG Digital Nomad and Remote Work visa options, 17 Jul 2026; EY Global Immigration Index: Remote Work and Digital Nomads, Mar 2026), neither of which lists this country; no official visa-type listing could be read, so no official verdict. The page sentences saying there is no such visa are consistent with that and were left alone. NOTE: EY (Mar 2026) names Senegal among countries "actively preparing to launch" a digital nomad visa in 2026; KPMG (17 Jul 2026) still lists none. The Dakar sentence ("as of mid-2026") is fine today but is the one most likely to go stale.

Serbia.note: No dedicated permit found in force. Caveat: Art. 40(4) of the Law on Foreigners lets the Government define categories by its own act and explicitly names 'stranci digitalni nomadi'; I found no implementing act, and the government's own Welcome to Serbia 'Digital nomads in Serbia' page names no permit (only tax relief). Remote workers use temporary residence on general grounds (e.g. self-employment).

Seychelles.note: Workcation Retreat Programme (launched 2021) status is unresolved. Official ICS permit pages list no remote-work permit; the Visitor's Permit is free for 3 months and extendable in 3-month blocks (SCR 5,000 each) to 12 months, for holiday, business or visiting. The SEBS application portal (seychelles.govtas.com) has no Workcation flow anywhere in its code. EY (Mar 2026) lists the programme as suspended 'according to the Seychelles Electronic Border System (SEBS) authorities'; KPMG (17 Jul 2026) still lists it (EUR 45, up to 1 year) without a source. The tourism board page (seychelles.travel) returned HTTP 522. The Mahe sentence matches the official position as far as it can be read, so no fix; but /nomad-visas still lists 'Workation Retreat' for Seychelles and should be re-checked.

Sierra Leone.note: Absence based only on two professional trackers (KPMG Digital Nomad and Remote Work visa options, 17 Jul 2026; EY Global Immigration Index: Remote Work and Digital Nomads, Mar 2026), neither of which lists this country; no official visa-type listing could be read, so no official verdict. The page sentences saying there is no such visa are consistent with that and were left alone.

Singapore.note: No MOM pass for remote work on foreign income. ONE Pass is a work pass for top earners (fixed monthly salary at least S$30,000), not a nomad visa. Both Singapore sentences correct.

Slovakia.note: Act 404/2011 on Residence of Foreigners, version in force from 1 July 2025, s.21: temporary-residence purposes are business, employment, study, special activity, research, family, armed-forces civilians, Slovaks abroad, long-term residents of another member state. No nomad purpose. Later (2026) consolidated versions could not be loaded.

Sri Lanka.note: Department of Immigration and Emigration, Residence Visa Division. For applicants 18+ in remote employment, freelancing or a business not registered in Sri Lanka serving clients abroad. Minimum monthly remittance USD 2,000 (plus USD 500 per dependant beyond two). Valid 1 year, renewable annually (renewal needs Inland Revenue tax registration). Fee USD 500 a year per person. Needs a Ministry of Digital Economy recommendation, police and medical clearance, international health insurance. No local employment. Launch reportedly early 2026 (date not on the official PDF). Both Sri Lanka sentences wrong.

Suriname.note: No digital nomad visa found; all sources to Sept 2026 agree. Not confirmed against an official category list.

Sweden.note: Migrationsverket: you need a work permit to work in Sweden whether employed in Sweden or abroad; no nomad permit.

Switzerland.note: SEM: no remote-work permit; third-country nationals need a permit for gainful activity in Switzerland, subject to labour-market admission conditions.

Taiwan.note: Bureau of Consular Affairs page created 2025-01-02: nationals of visa-exempt countries only; proof of remote work; either a digital nomad visa from another country, or annual salary of at least US$40,000 (age 30+) / US$20,000 (age 20-29) in one of the last two years; average bank balance at least US$10,000 a month over six months; health insurance; qualifications reviewed by the National Development Council. Can also be applied for inside Taiwan at BOCA or the MOFA Central, Southern, Southwestern or Eastern Taiwan offices. Length of stay not stated on the page read.

Tajikistan.note: MFA Consular Department lists 16 visa categories; none for remote work.

Tanzania.note: Official e-visa guidelines: "Tanzania Immigration Services issues six types of visa" (ordinary, multiple, business, transit and others); none is for remote work, and ordinary visa holders "are not required to work or conduct any business". Not in either tracker.

Thailand.note: Royal Thai MFA: DTV is "specially designed for foreigners who are on a tourist trip and working remotely"; purpose 1 is "Workcation (digital nomad/remote worker/foreign talent/freelancer)". Multiple entry, valid 5 years, each stay up to 180 days, extendable once in-country. Financial evidence at least 500,000 THB (MFA visa types list https://image.mfa.go.th/mfa/0/SRBviAC5gs/PPT-TypesofVisa_18.06.2025.pdf). Fees vary by embassy. Introduced 2024.

Timor-Leste.note: Migration and Asylum Law 11/2017 (amended by Law 10/2021) visa types: courtesy, transit, tourism, airport transit, work, business, temporary stay, residence. No nomad category.

Togo.note: Absence based only on two professional trackers (KPMG Digital Nomad and Remote Work visa options, 17 Jul 2026; EY Global Immigration Index: Remote Work and Digital Nomads, Mar 2026), neither of which lists this country; no official visa-type listing could be read, so no official verdict. The page sentences saying there is no such visa are consistent with that and were left alone.

Trinidad and Tobago.note: No remote-work or digital nomad visa found in any source.

Tunisia.note: Absence based only on two professional trackers (KPMG Digital Nomad and Remote Work visa options, 17 Jul 2026; EY Global Immigration Index: Remote Work and Digital Nomads, Mar 2026), neither of which lists this country; no official visa-type listing could be read, so no official verdict. The page sentences saying there is no such visa are consistent with that and were left alone. Sfax side claim "Tunisia has discussed one for several years" not verified.

Turkey.visa: Digital Nomad Visa (first step: Digital Nomad Identification Certificate)
Turkey.note: Official GoTurkiye platform (Ministry of Culture and Tourism / TGA): the Digital Nomad Identification Certificate "is the first step in the process of obtaining Digital Nomad Visa to Turkiye"; you then "apply for Digital Nomad Visa at Turkiye Visa center/consulate". Requirements: age 21 to 55; university degree; contract with a non-Turkish company, or if self-employed a contract with non-Turkish companies; "a monthly income of 3,000 USD or 36,000 USD annually"; passport valid 6 months. Eligible: 36 nationalities (26 EU states, all but Cyprus, plus Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, UK, Switzerland, USA, Canada, Russia, Ukraine, Belarus). Page title adds "and short-term residence". Launch year and visa length are NOT stated on the official page (KPMG/EY list the visa; the site row says up to 1 year). So every sentence saying Turkey has no digital nomad visa "as such" contradicts the official naming.

Turkmenistan.note: MFA consular pages describe single, multiple and transit visas only; no remote-work category. Weakest evidence: the Law on Migration itself was not read.

Turks and Caicos.note: No remote-work or digital nomad programme; never introduced. No TCI immigration page listing permit types could be reached, so absence rests on the government portal plus consistent secondary sources (visittci.com).

UAE.note: Remote-work residence visa exists (KPMG 17 Jul 2026; EY Mar 2026). The official pages (investindubai.gov.ae, u.ae) blocked automated fetches (403 / connection refused), so its terms were NOT verified here. The Dubai sentence is not an absence-of-nomad-visa claim (it says freelancers with UAE clients need a licence or permit setup); judged defensible and left alone, but the freelancer Green visa route could not be checked on u.ae.

Uganda.note: Absence based only on two professional trackers (KPMG Digital Nomad and Remote Work visa options, 17 Jul 2026; EY Global Immigration Index: Remote Work and Digital Nomads, Mar 2026), neither of which lists this country; no official visa-type listing could be read, so no official verdict. The page sentences saying there is no such visa are consistent with that and were left alone.

United Kingdom.note: No digital nomad or remote-work route in the Immigration Rules. Since the HC 246 changes (in force 31 January 2024) a Standard Visitor may do remote work for an overseas employer only if it is not the main purpose of the visit; visitors get up to six months.

United States.note: No digital nomad or remote-work category exists in US immigration law. Visitors enter on the Visa Waiver Program (ESTA, 90 days, not extendable) or a B-1/B-2 visa; employment is not permitted on either. Statements about pending legislation ('none under active legislation', 'none expected', 'no proposal close to enactment') were not checked against congress.gov and are left as editorial. Only Boise is fixed, because 'no intention of creating one' is an unverifiable claim about intent.

Uzbekistan.note: No digital nomad category. The IT-visa (Minister of Digital Technologies order No. 3387-1, in force 7 March 2026) needs an IT Park / ministry recommendation and, for specialists, a Uzbek employer; it is not a remote-work visa.

Vietnam.note: Law No. 118/2025/QH15 (effective 1 July 2026) added preferential visa types UD1/UD2 for high-quality digital-technology workforce and other preferred groups: a talent/employment category, not remote work on foreign income. No digital nomad visa.

Zambia.note: Department of Immigration permit types: residence, employment, investors, spouse, study, diplomatic, visiting, cross border, temporary employment, temporary, transit, asylum seeker. No remote-work permit. Not in either tracker.

Zimbabwe.note: Absence based only on two professional trackers (KPMG Digital Nomad and Remote Work visa options, 17 Jul 2026; EY Global Immigration Index: Remote Work and Digital Nomads, Mar 2026), neither of which lists this country; no official visa-type listing could be read, so no official verdict.
